title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space (Word2Vec)
inputs: A large text corpus (sequence of words/tokens)
outputs: Continuous vector representations (embeddings) for each word in the vocabulary
pseudocode:
1. Initialize word vectors V[vocab_size, dim] randomly
2. For each epoch:
3.   For each word w_t in corpus:
4.     Extract context words within window [t-C, t+C]
5.     # CBOW approach:
6.     context_vec = mean(V[context_words])
7.     Predict w_t from context_vec using hierarchical softmax or negative sampling
8.     Update V[context_words] and V[w_t] via gradient descent
9.     # Skip-gram approach (alternative):
10.    For each context word w_c in window:
11.      Predict w_c from V[w_t] using hierarchical softmax or negative sampling
12.      Update V[w_t] and V[w_c] via gradient descent
13. Return trained word vectors V
key_equations: CBOW objective: maximize p(w_t | context) = softmax(V[w_t]^T * mean(V[context]))
Skip-gram objective: maximize product of p(w_c | w_t) for all context words w_c
Negative sampling loss: log σ(v'_{w_O}^T v_{w_I}) + Σ_{i=1}^k E_{w_i~P_n(w)} [log σ(-v'_{w_i}^T v_{w_I})]
Hierarchical softmax: p(w|context) = product of σ(sign(path_j) * v'_j^T h) along binary tree path
Training complexity: Q_CBOW = N×D + D×log_2(V), Q_Skip-gram = C×(D + D×log_2(V))
evaluation_dataset: Google News corpus (6B tokens, 1M vocabulary), also tested on Semantic-Syntactic Word Relationship test set (8869 semantic + 10675 syntactic questions)
toy_dataset_suggestion: text8 dataset (100MB of cleaned Wikipedia text, ~17M tokens) or a small subset (first 1-10MB). Alternatively, the Brown corpus or a subset of WikiText-2 for quick laptop training.
key_figure_description: Table showing word analogy task accuracy (semantic and syntactic) vs. vector dimensionality and training data size. X-axis: training corpus size (e.g., 24M, 49M, 98M words). Y-axis: accuracy percentage on analogy task (e.g., 'king - man + woman ≈ queen'). Multiple curves for different embedding dimensions (50, 100, 300, 600). Shows that both dimension and data size improve accuracy with diminishing returns.
notes: For toy implementation: (1) Use Skip-gram with negative sampling (simpler than hierarchical softmax). (2) Train on small corpus (1-10MB text) for 1-3 epochs. (3) Evaluate on a subset of word analogy questions (e.g., 100-500 pairs). (4) Skip distributed training and AdaGrad; use simple SGD with linear learning rate decay. (5) Focus on demonstrating that learned vectors capture semantic relationships (king-man+woman≈queen) rather than achieving SOTA accuracy. (6) Use vocabulary of most frequent 5k-30k words instead of 1M. (7) Verify embeddings via cosine similarity and simple analogy tests rather than full benchmark.
